entry.title: Attenuation and half-value layer: interactive simulator
entry.summary: With a half-value layer of 2 cm and 6 cm of material, the model transmits 1/8, or 12.5%. Double the thickness to see exponential decay.

entry.title: Food cooling: Biot number and core temperature
entry.summary: With h = 25 W/m²/K, Lc = 0.02 m and λ = 0.5 W/m/K, Bi = 1: internal gradients matter. Compare surface and core temperatures.

entry.title: Heat engine and Carnot limit: cycle and energy balance
entry.summary: Between 400 °C and 20 °C, the Carnot limit is about 56.5%: at most 564.5 J of work from 1000 J of heat. Follow the cycle.

entry.title: Chi-square test: observed counts, expected counts and contributions
entry.summary: For 120 throws of a fair die, expect 20 per face. Change one face and see its contribution to χ²; also the 2×2 table of the course.

entry.title: Compton scattering: angle and energy sharing
entry.summary: At 255.5 keV and 180°, the photon keeps 127.75 keV and the electron receives the same. Set the angle and follow the energy split.

entry.title: Correlation, significance and R²: distinguish the concepts
entry.summary: With r = 0.10, R² stays at 1% while the p-value falls from 0.599 to 0.0015 between n = 30 and n = 1000. Separate the two ideas.

entry.title: Electromagnetic wave: electric and magnetic fields
entry.summary: At 50 MHz in vacuum, the wavelength is about 6 m and the period 20 ns. Follow the E and B fields of a plane wave, step by step.

entry.title: Freezing: sensible heat, latent heat and power
entry.summary: With total energy unchanged, doubling the duration halves the average power. Isolate the contribution of latent heat.

entry.title: Regression and an influential point: move an observation
entry.summary: Move the orange point, then turn it off: the line, r and the p-value change. One observation can weigh heavily.

entry.title: Interactive normal distribution: area, probability and z-score
entry.summary: At z = 1.96 the left area is about 0.975; from −1.96 to +1.96, about 95%. Convert a value to a probability, or the reverse.

entry.title: Refrigeration: coefficient of performance and Carnot limit
entry.summary: Between −10 °C and +40 °C the maximum COP is 5.26; between −40 °C and +20 °C, 3.89. See why a larger temperature gap costs more.

entry.title: Regression: confidence interval and prediction interval
entry.summary: For n = 20 and se = 1, the half-width is 0.47 for the mean and 2.15 for a future observation. Move x₀ and compare.

entry.title: Interactive ROC curve: sensitivity, specificity and prevalence
entry.summary: The threshold moves the point on the ROC curve. Prevalence leaves sensitivity and specificity unchanged but changes predictive values.

entry.title: Interactive t-test: means, variability and p-values
entry.summary: Same difference, same variability, more patients: the p-value changes. Pooled-variance Student test for two treatments at the 5% level.

entry.title: The Sun, the seasons and the clock: one time for every measurement

entry.title: Scientific publishing: no verification of data and code, no trust

entry.summary: Le rayonnement diffus est l'une des composantes les plus difficiles de la ressource solaire, surtout là où aérosols, humidité et contrastes climatiques sont forts. Mesure et prévision de la fraction diffuse en Arabie saoudite, avec un modèle hybride par empilement.

entry.title: Revisiting Persistence: Symmetry-Constrained Forecasting of Periodically Correlated Energy Processes
entry.summary: This work revisits persistence forecasting (repeating the last observation) for periodically varying statistics, including the daily cycle of solar irradiance. BLEND combines the latest observation with an observation aligned to the target phase of the cycle.

entry.title: Revisiter la persistance : BLEND, une prévision sous contrainte de symétrie pour les processus énergétiques périodiques
entry.summary: La persistance revisitée pour les séries à statistiques périodiques, comme le cycle journalier de l'éclairement solaire. BLEND combine la dernière observation et l'observation alignée sur la même phase du cycle. La persistance est la prévision qui recopie la dernière valeur connue.

entry.title: From Pixels to Tolerances: Rethinking Forecast Validation with the γ-Index
entry.summary: Classical metrics like RMSE (root mean squared error) evaluate forecasts as if every pixel must match perfectly in space and time. Machines optimize for that. Humans do not think that way.

entry.title: Des pixels aux tolérances : valider les prévisions avec l'indice γ
entry.summary: Les métriques classiques comme la RMSE (racine de l'erreur quadratique moyenne) jugent une prévision comme si chaque pixel devait coïncider parfaitement dans l'espace et le temps. L'indice γ accepte un décalage toléré, comme le fait un expert.

entry.title: Métriques NICEᵏ : un cadre unifié pour évaluer les prévisions solaires déterministes

Les métriques NICEᵏ rapportent les erreurs à celles d'une référence explicite, la persistance (qui recopie la dernière valeur connue).

entry.title: A Simple Method for Quickly Estimating Solar Irradiance Forecast Errors
entry.summary: Researchers have developed linear models that predict solar irradiance forecast errors using only solar variability at a specific location.
